title: Backflow preventer leaking: relief valve, top or body?
description: Locate a backflow preventer leak, compare continuous and intermittent RPZ discharge with FEBCO guidance, and distinguish PVB and double-check symptoms before repair.
prompt: Where is the water coming from?
answer: A brief release can be different from continuous discharge. The useful clues are the exact opening, whether flow stops, recent freezing or service, and visible body damage.
urgency: Continuous discharge, flooding, freezing, or a cracked body needs prompt professional attention. Never plug a relief or vent opening.
diagramAlt: RPZ diagram marking the lower relief vent and body joints as observation points
identifiers: Relief opening: water exits an intentional opening below the assembly.
Body or joint: water appears at a crack, fitting, test cock, or cover.
Downstream drain-down: a short release happens around irrigation start or shutdown.

choices.label: From the relief vent, continuously
choices.detail: Possible fouling, pressure condition, or internal failure; do not cap the opening.

choices.label: From a crack or split body
choices.detail: Freeze or impact damage can make replacement more likely.

choices.label: Only briefly during a cycle
choices.detail: Record duration and frequency before deciding it is normal or faulty.

choices.label: From a threaded fitting or test cock
choices.detail: A localized external leak still needs the correct isolation and service procedure.

steps.title: Mark the exit point
steps.body: Take a short video that includes the full device and the exact point where water begins.

steps.title: Record the timing
steps.body: Note continuous, intermittent, irrigation start, shutdown, overnight, or freeze/thaw behavior.

steps.title: Check the compliance consequence
steps.body: Repair or replacement may need a passing retest and accepted report before the utility record closes.

safeChecks: Check for visible cracks and ice without touching a pressurized assembly.
Record recent valve work, water shutoffs, irrigation changes, or freezing weather.
If you know the correct upstream shutoff and can operate it safely, follow the property emergency procedure.
stopConditions: Flow is forceful or cannot be contained
Water can reach electrical equipment or create ice
The device serves fire protection or a critical commercial process
notThisDevice: Water from a pressure-regulator bell or adjustment screw is a different problem.
Water at a hose faucet may come from a hose-bib vacuum breaker.
Wastewater backup is a sewer backwater problem.

related.title: What happens after a failed test

evidenceNote: Likely causes are presented as possibilities, not remote diagnoses. Manufacturer instructions and a qualified local professional control service work.

fieldSections.title: Start with the outlet, not a guessed repair kit.
fieldSections.introduction: Use the visible location to choose a narrower guide. A working description helps a technician; it does not establish a remote diagnosis.

rows.meaning: Possible relief discharge; observe whether it is brief, intermittent, or continuous.
rows.nextStep: Use the relief-discharge guide and preserve drainage.

rows.meaning: The air inlet, bonnet, and startup sequence need a different check from RPZ discharge.
rows.nextStep: Record timing through one irrigation cycle.

rows.observation: Double-check cover, test port, or shutoff
rows.meaning: Locate the external wet point separately from any failed internal check.
A hose-end vacuum breaker is a different product family.
rows.nextStep: Confirm the attachment label and vent location.

rows.observation: Cracked body, flooding, or unknown isolation
rows.meaning: The immediate priority is containing damage through a known safe procedure.
rows.nextStep: Get qualified local help; include the device photo and system use.

fieldSections.diagramAlt: Conceptual RPZ observation points with relief outlet and check covers
fieldSections.caption: For an RPZ only. Compare the PVB and double-check paths when these features do not match.

fieldSections.title: RPZ relief discharge: timing changes the investigation.
fieldSections.introduction: The FEBCO 825Y / LF825Y manual separates continuous from intermittent discharge. These are model-specific troubleshooting possibilities for qualified service, not a diagnosis from a video.

rows.meaning: The 825Y manual lists debris at check seating surfaces or the relief seat. Seeing water at the relief outlet does not isolate the faulty component.
rows.nextStep: Provide a full-device photo, exact model/size and a video showing whether discharge stops.

rows.meaning: The same manual lists inlet-pressure fluctuations and downstream surges. Replacing only relief parts may miss the system condition.
rows.nextStep: Record whether events coincide with irrigation, pumps, shutoffs or other water use.

rows.meaning: An external pressure-boundary leak is separate evidence from water leaving the designed relief path.
rows.nextStep: Mark the point where water first appears; use the repair-versus-replace route if the body is damaged.

rows.meaning: The drainage route and consequences need attention alongside the assembly’s condition.
rows.nextStep: Keep the outlet open; have the site’s qualified team assess drainage and safe isolation.

caseStudies.title: UMass Life Sciences: plan for RPZ discharge
caseStudies.constraint: Lower-level research spaces were vulnerable to water from large RPZ assemblies.
caseStudies.documentedAction: Watts reports that engineers specified 113-6RFP flood-protection shutdown valves upstream of large RPZs to address the drainage risk.
caseStudies.planningLesson: Assess where discharged water can go and what it can damage. This is a prevention project, not a documented diagnosis of a leaking valve; its design is not a retrofit recommendation for your site.

questions.question: Is water from an RPZ relief valve always a broken relief valve?
questions.answer: No. The FEBCO 825Y / LF825Y manual includes check-seat debris as well as relief-seat debris for continuous discharge. A qualified test and service assessment must distinguish the component and system conditions.

questions.question: Can intermittent discharge be ignored if it stops?
questions.answer: Record it and arrange assessment if it recurs. The 825Y manual identifies inlet fluctuations and downstream surges as possibilities; stopping by itself does not prove that the assembly passes a test.

questions.question: Why does a backflow preventer leak after freezing?
questions.answer: A visible crack or distorted pressure boundary changes the scope. Do not assume a rubber kit repairs a damaged body. Show the model and damaged area to the repairer and compare replacement, test and reporting requirements.

questions.question: Can I cap the vent to stop the leak?
questions.answer: Keep intentional relief and air-inlet openings unobstructed. For flooding, use only the property’s known safe emergency procedure; fire protection or critical process systems require coordinated qualified response.

questions.question: What should I include in a leak repair request?
questions.answer: Include a wide photo, label/size, exact exit point, timing, recent work or freezing, protected system and any failed-test report. Ask for diagnosis, correct parts, test after service, and the local report/acceptance scope separately.
